A Sankey (or alluvial) diagram shows how a quantity **flows through a sequence of categorical
stages** — patients moving from a cohort, to a treatment, to an outcome; or reads from a sample, to
a mapping status, to a feature. The width of each stream is the magnitude. Here we build one in
Python with [canvasxpress](https://pypi.org/project/canvasxpress/) — interactive and reproducible.

## Install

```bash
pip install canvasxpress
```

## The data shape

canvasXpress builds a Sankey from a table where **each row is one path** through the stages, plus a
frequency/weight. Swap this simulated clinical flow for your own counts.

```{python}
import random
random.seed(1)

cohorts  = ["Cohort A", "Cohort B"]
treats   = ["Drug 1", "Drug 2", "Placebo"]
outcomes = ["Response", "Stable", "Progression"]

Cohort, Treatment, Outcome, Freq = [], [], [], []
for co in cohorts:
    for tr in treats:
        for ou in outcomes:
            base = 40 if ou == "Response" else 25 if ou == "Stable" else 15
            if tr == "Placebo" and ou == "Response":
                base = 12                                   # placebo responds less
            Cohort.append(co); Treatment.append(tr); Outcome.append(ou)
            Freq.append(base + random.randint(0, 15))
```

The value (`Freq`) is the single measured variable; the stage columns are sample annotations (`x`).

```{python}
from canvasxpress.canvas import CanvasXpress
from canvasxpress.render.jupyter import CXNoteBook
from IPython.display import display

ids = [f"r{i+1}" for i in range(len(Freq))]
data = {
    "y": {"vars": ["Freq"], "smps": ids, "data": [Freq]},
    "x": {"Cohort": Cohort, "Treatment": Treatment, "Outcome": Outcome},
}

config = {
    "graphType": "Sankey",
    "sankeyAxes": ["Cohort", "Treatment", "Outcome"],
    "xAxis": ["Freq"],
    "colorBy": "Outcome",
    "sankeyType": "proportional",
    "graphOrientation": "horizontal",
    "title": "Patient flow: cohort to treatment to outcome",
}

cx = CanvasXpress(render_to="sankey", data=data, config=config, width=700, height=500)
for part in CXNoteBook(cx).render():
    display(part)
```

Hover any stream to see the count; the widths are proportional to the frequency, so you can read the
flow at a glance. `sankeyType` can also be `"aligned"` (classic alluvial) or `"equal"`.

## Why "reproducible"

The `data`+`config` **is** the figure — one portable JSON spec. The same spec renders the identical
Sankey from R or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later.
